prompt: The client asks: "Which cost-cutting option should we pursue first?" Fact sheet: renegotiating suppliers saves $8M a year and takes 6 months; closing two plants saves $15M a year, takes 2 years and costs $20M up front; cutting marketing saves $5M but risks sales; the target is $10M of savings this year; the company has 5,000 employees. Which is the best recommendation?

options.text: It saves $8M within 6 months with no up-front cost, most of this year's $10M target; plant closures save more but take 2 years and cost $20M up front. The main risk is that suppliers push back and savings come in below $8M. Putting it together, start with supplier renegotiation.
options.feedback: The answer comes last. Lead with the recommendation, then support it.
